item.title: Bring Me Flesh: Twas the night before Christmas, and inside the shed, was a pile of upvotes, all stacked on a sled
item.content:encoded: The odd phrases in the parentheses adds the essential layer of surrealism to this, which is why I loved seeing this. I was already going to upvote when I was done reading, but the "Naught but dust" made me scroll up and give a +1. Normally, perspective tales on a hostile anomaly have a strangely-edgy atmosphere that I don't usually care for, but this one adds a well-crafted, alien-like mindset to the creature, and also does it well.

item.title: SCP-5251: Ohh THAT'S WHY its named Flax!
item.content:encoded:
FINALLY IT MAKES SO MUCH SENSE

Spoilers!
You've been warned!

From Wikipedia: "In early versions of Sleeping Beauty….the princess pricks her finger, not with a spindle, but with a sliver of flax, which later is sucked out by her children conceived as she sleeps."

Petrov is Sleeping Beauty here. Getting pricked by the Flaxseed (the Skip) and doomed to be "asleep" to the world forever

Definitely want to try my first declass on the subreddit with this one, as I think I've finally got most of the pieces together. And it all came from finding what flax meant…..

Beautiful article, Croq. You've given us a masterclass on "what is not said is as important as what is".

item.title: SCP-3150:
item.content:encoded:
I made a correction which I invite the author to evaluate.

Ah, I must go totoo.

This use of "too" makes sense in context, but it is possible that the proper correction is "I must go to [destination]" and the destination was not entered. If this is the case, please revise my correction. Thanks, and thanks for writing a very engaging scip.

item.title: SCP-3149: I really *want* to like this...
item.content:encoded:
…and I'll upvote it, but the heavy-handed depiction of Westhead Media was a little too unsubtle for my taste, and there are asides that feel like plot holes. For example, the nutrient mix that stimulates creativity is either anomalous or non-anomalous; since we as readers are aware that it doesn't exist in the real world, we should receive a little more information about it, to clarify whether the supplement is an everyday vitamin in the world of SCP-3149 or an unusual product that everyday people would find as astonishing as an anomaly.

So, +1, but with reservations. I feel like this could easily be improved by an order of magnitude with a manageable amount of revision.

item.title: SCP-4666:
item.content:encoded:
Was inspired by PeppersGhost 's recent tale to come take a second look at this. (BTW the tale is quite well done, pls go look at it.)

I just don't get the hype with this, and the feeling has only gotten stronger as time wears on. It's a creepy inversion of Santa. That's all there is, beyond some very creative squick. And the quick is very good, but there doesn't seem to be anything driving it. That tone even extends to the character itself, creating the impression that Santa really is just bustin' heads for shock value. Even the addendum, which was an excellent chance to round out the narrative and give us a finishing reveal, just adds more gore and Santa comparisons. It's like drinking from a fire hose, but the fire hose is spouting children's body parts and pine resin. It's frustratingly shallow once you push past it all.

That being said, I guess it's really effective at what it's trying to do and be. Can't argue with that.
